cases.statement: One family (35958611, Family 1): the proband P1 (V:24) and three carriers with isolated recurrent oral ulcers (mother IV:14, sisters V:22 and V:26). 37342083 re-reports the same family from Tian et al., 2022 (= 35958611) in its review table; its proband row merged with P1, but its mother and two sisters received new identities.

people.label: P1 (V:24)
people.key_phenotypes: onset at 18 years with recurrent high fever; oral and genital ulcers from 22; erythema nodosum and panniculitis; nonbacterial osteomyelitis of the tibias; old bilateral uveitis on examination

quotes.quote: The proband (V:24, Figure 1A) of the first family (P1) was a 28-year-old Chinese Han woman.
A heterozygous A547T mutation was found in the proband of the first family, which is characterized by a G to A substitution in exon 7, resulting in missense alanine-to-threonine exchange.
At 18 years of age, she had recurrent high fever lasting several weeks once every half a year without obvious triggers.
She had recurrent oral and genital ulcers from the age of 22.
In recent years, she also suffered from recurrent erythema nodosa (Figure 1B) and subcutaneous nodules, which were pathologically diagnosed as panniculitis.
Nonbacterial osteomyelitis was found in her tibias via bone scan and biopsy.
She had no ocular symptoms, but ophthalmic examination suggested the presence of old uveitis in both eyes.

phenotype_specificity.statement: The proband was studied by WES. The authors consider her features typical of HA20 (oral and genital ulcers, fever, arthritis, uveitis). WES also found a paternal heterozygous NOD2 variant; the authors judged her features not consistent with Blau syndrome. No other genes are reported as excluded.

quotes.quote: Whole-exome sequencing (WES) by next-generation sequencing was performed in the Center for Genetic Testing, Joy Orient Translational Medicine Research Centre Co., Ltd., Beijing, China.

We consider A547T to be a novel variant in HA20 because of the typical manifestations of HA20 in the proband of the first family, including oral and genital ulcers, fever, arthritis and uveitis, and a minor allele frequency of < 0.0001 of this variant in the Asian population.

Interestingly, we identified a paternal heterozygous NOD2 A192 V variant in this patient, but her father had no symptoms of Blau syndrome, and her manifestations were not consistent with Blau syndrome.

segregation.statement: Three relatives with isolated recurrent oral ulcers (mother, two sisters) carry the variant. The father (IV:13) is asymptomatic; his TNFAIP3 genotype is not stated in the text (he is the source of the NOD2 variant). Parents of the proband's maternal line are cousins.

quotes.quote: Her mother (IV:14) and her two sisters (V:22, V:26) had recurrent oral ulcers, without arthritis, vulvar ulcers, erythema nodosa or uveitis.
Genetic analysis confirmed the presence of the TNFAIP3 A547T variant in her symptomatic mother and sisters.
Her father (IV:13) had no symptoms.
Pedigree analysis (Figure 1A) showed that the proband’s grandmother (III:2) and maternal grandfather (III:3) were cousins.

functional.statement: No wet-lab functional study of this variant: the authors state functional studies were not done for personal reasons of the patient, and the 37342083 review states no in vitro functional test was performed. (A 3D homology model is listed under computational_predictions.)

quotes.quote: Due to the lack of functional studies for personal reasons of the patient, the accurate pathogenic significance of A547T was indeed unknown.
The variations p.(Val377Met), p.(Met476Ile), and p.(Ala547Thr) are considered of uncertain significance as no in vitro functional test was performed to assess their pathogenicity.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense substitution, p.(Ala547Thr), in exon 7; 37342083 places it in ZnF3 (from the batch HGVS and the papers). The papers describe HA20 as caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants.

quotes.quote: Haploinsufficiency of A20 (HA20) is a newly described rare autoinflammatory disease that resembles BS and is caused by heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in the TNF alpha induced protein 3 (TNFAIP3) gene (3, 4).
A heterozygous A547T mutation was found in the proband of the first family, which is characterized by a G to A substitution in exon 7, resulting in missense alanine-to-threonine exchange.
| Znf2 | Znf3 | Znf4 | Between Znf4 and Znf5 | Znf6 |

computational_predictions.statement: I-TASSER homology model: altered hydrogen bond with residue 551 (distance 2.1 vs 2.2). 37342083 Table 2: CADD 8.432; residue 'Poorly conserved' (tenth variant column).

quotes.quote: To understand the significance of missense mutation A547T to the structure of A20, three-dimensional (3D) structure homology models of the A20 protein encoded by the wild type and A547T variant (Figure 2A) were predicted using the I-TASSER online server (25), and the architecture was visualized using PyMOL Viewer software.

The replacement of residue 547 from alanine to threonine resulted in altered hydrogen bond interactions (hydrogen bond distance: WT: 2.1, A547T: 2.2) with residue 551 and the overall three-dimensional structure of the protein.

authors_classification.statement: 35958611 contradicts itself: the Abstract says the variant was 'validated to be pathogenic', the Results say it 'had never been validated', and the Discussion says its significance 'was indeed unknown'. 37342083 classifies it as of uncertain significance (Table 2 and text).

quotes.quote: Two novel variants, A547T and c.1906+2T>G, were validated to be pathogenic in our study.
Among the three TNFAIP3 variants detected in these HA20 patients, two novel variants, A547T and c.1906+2T>G, had never been validated to be pathogenic.
Due to the lack of functional studies for personal reasons of the patient, the accurate pathogenic significance of A547T was indeed unknown.
The variations p.(Val377Met), p.(Met476Ile), and p.(Ala547Thr) are considered of uncertain significance as no in vitro functional test was performed to assess their pathogenicity.

concerns: Same people recorded twice: 37342083 Table 2 column 10 is a review summary of Tian et al., 2022, which is 35958611. Its mother and two sisters (HA20-ID0630, HA20-ID0636, HA20-ID0637) are the same people as IV:14, V:22 and V:26 (HA20-ID0201, HA20-ID0205, HA20-ID0206). The proband rows are already merged (HA20-ID0202).
Numbering: 35958611 names the proband V:24 in the text; the batch label is 'P1'. The batch also has IV:14 (her mother) as a separate row, so check that IV:14 is not mistaken for the proband.

35958611 contradicts itself on the authors' assessment (Abstract vs Results vs Discussion). It also contradicts itself on the proband's features: the text reports recurrent genital ulcers, but Table 1 row 1 marks genital ulcers '–'; the text says joint pain 'without joint swelling', while Table 1 marks arthritis '+'.
Second variant in the proband: a paternal heterozygous NOD2 A192V variant (another gene).
The relatives' phenotype is limited to recurrent oral ulcers; the proband's features include nonbacterial osteomyelitis and panniculitis.
Transcript: the papers use NM_006290.4 / NM_006290; the batch uses NM_001270508.2. Positions as written agree with the batch prediction (protein_check: agrees).
notes_for_panel: One family with four carriers, reported in 35958611 and re-summarised in 37342083. No wet-lab functional data. Watch for duplicate identities of the three relatives and for the internal contradictions in 35958611.
